title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 6. Beholding Mahavana and Other Places
html:
Crossing the Yamuna, Krishnadasa shows the Lord Mahavana and Nanda's house — the places of Krishna's childhood pastimes: the liberation of Putana, the binding of Damodara, the broken Arjuna trees; Gokula, Gopeshvara, Sapta-samudra, the houses of Ayana, Ananda and Upananda; the story of Nanda handing Krishna to a gopi on a stormy day moves the Lord; the sarga ends with Vraja moving to Bhadraka and Bhandira

Verse 1

एवं संकथयन् विप्रो भानुजां प्रभुणा समम्।
उत्तीर्य दर्शयामास नन्दगेहं महावनम्॥१॥

evaṁ saṁkathayan vipro bhānujāṁ prabhuṇā samam|
uttīrya darśayāmāsa nandagehaṁ mahāvanam||1||

evam — thus; samkathayan — conversing; viprah — the brahmana; bhanu-jam — the daughter of the Sun; prabhuna — with the Lord; samam — together; uttirya — crossing; darshayam asa — showed; nanda-geham — the house of Nanda; maha-vanam — Mahavana.

1Conversing thus, the brahmana crossed the daughter of the Sun together with the Lord and showed Him the house of Nanda — Mahavana.

Verse 2

पूतनामोक्षणं चात्र शकटस्य विमोचनम्।
तृणावर्तस्य दुर्वृत्तेर्हरिणात्र कृतो वधः॥२॥

pūtanāmokṣaṇaṁ cātra śakaṭasya vimocanam|
tṛṇāvartasya durvṛtterhariṇātra kṛto vadhaḥ||2||

putana-mokshanam — the liberation of Putana; cha — and; atra — here; shakatasya — of the cart; vimochanam — the shattering; trinavartasya — of Trinavarta; durvritteh — the wicked; harina — by Hari; atra — here; kritah — was done; vadhah — the slaying.

2"Here Putana attained liberation, here the cart was shattered, here Hari slew the wicked Trinavarta1.

Verse 3

जृम्भमाणेन कृष्णेन चोदरे विश्वमद्भुतम्।
दर्शितमत्र मात्रे सा भीताप्याशिषमाददौ॥३॥

jṛmbhamāṇena kṛṣṇena codare viśvamadbhutam|
darśitamatra mātre sā bhītāpyāśiṣamādadau||3||

jrimbhamanena — yawning; krishnena — by Krishna; cha — and; udare — in His belly; vishvam — the universe; adbhutam — wondrous; darshitam — was shown; atra — here; matre — to His mother; sa — she; bhita — frightened; api — though; ashisham — blessing; adadau — gave.

3Here Krishna, yawning, showed His mother the wondrous universe within His belly, and she, though frightened, gave Him her blessing.

Verse 4

अत्रैव नामकरणं गर्गेण विहितं किल।
मृत्तिकाभक्षणं चात्र विश्वरूपप्रदर्शनम्॥४॥

atraiva nāmakaraṇaṁ gargeṇa vihitaṁ kila|
mṛttikābhakṣaṇaṁ cātra viśvarūpapradarśanam||4||

atra — here; eva — indeed; nama-karanam — the name-giving rite; gargena — by Garga; vihitam — was performed; kila — it is said; mrittika-bhakshanam — the eating of clay; cha — and; atra — here; vishva-rupa-pradarshanam — the showing of the universal form.

4Here too, it is said, Garga performed the name-giving rite2; here Krishna ate clay and revealed the universal form.

Verse 5

दधिमन्थनदण्डं हि धृतवान् हि हरिः स्वयम्।
मातृहर्षाय भगवान् नर्तितुं ह्युपचक्रमे॥५॥

dadhimanthanadaṇḍaṁ hi dhṛtavān hi hariḥ svayam|
mātṛharṣāya bhagavān nartituṁ hyupacakrame||5||

dadhi-manthana-dandam — the churning-rod for curd; hi — indeed; dhritavan — held; hi — indeed; harih — Hari; svayam — Himself; matri-harshaya — for His mother's joy; bhagavan — the Lord; nartitum — to dance; hi — indeed; upachakrame — began.

5Here Hari Himself held the churning-rod for the curd; here the Lord would begin to dance to delight His mother.

Verse 6

यशोदा तं क्रोडे कृत्वा हसन्ती वीक्ष्य तन्मुखम्।
स्तनं संपाययामास कौतूहलसमन्विता॥६॥

yaśodā taṁ kroḍe kṛtvā hasantī vīkṣya tanmukham|
stanaṁ saṁpāyayāmāsa kautūhalasamanvitā||6||

yashoda — Yashoda; tam — Him; krode — on her lap; kritva — taking; hasanti — laughing; vikshya — looking at; tat-mukham — His face; stanam — the breast; sampayayam asa — gave to suck; kautuhala-samanvita — full of delight.

6Yashoda took Him on her lap, laughed as she gazed at His face, and, full of tenderness, gave Him the breast.

Verse 7

दुग्धमुत्तापनं वीक्ष्य तं स्थाप्य सत्वरं सती।
चुल्लीस्थं दुग्धमुत्तार्य प्रायान्मन्थनसंस्थितम्॥७॥

dugdhamuttāpanaṁ vīkṣya taṁ sthāpya satvaraṁ satī|
cullīsthaṁ dugdhamuttārya prāyānmanthanasaṁsthitam||7||

dugdham — the milk; uttapanam — boiling over; vikshya — seeing; tam — Him; sthapya — putting down; satvaram — quickly; sati — the good woman; chulli-stham — standing on the hearth; dugdham — the milk; uttarya — taking off; prayat — went; manthana-samsthitam — to the place of churning.

7Seeing the milk boiling over, the good woman quickly set Him down, took the milk off the hearth and went back to her churning3.

Verse 8

कृष्णोऽपि क्रोधेन समन्वितः स्वयं
भाण्डं च भित्त्वा दृषदश्मना किल।
गृहं प्रविष्टो नवनीतकं चा-
शित्वोलूखलाङ्घ्र्युपरि स्थितो हसन्॥८॥

kṛṣṇo'pi krodhena samanvitaḥ svayaṁ
bhāṇḍaṁ ca bhittvā dṛṣadaśmanā kila|
gṛhaṁ praviṣṭo navanītakaṁ cā-
śitvolūkhalāṅghryupari sthito hasan||8||

krishnah — Krishna; api — for His part; krodhena — with anger; samanvitah — filled; svayam — Himself; bhandam — the pot; cha — and; bhittva — breaking; drishat-ashmana — with a stone; kila — they say; griham — the house; pravishtah — entering; navanitakam — fresh butter; cha — and; ashitva — eating; ulukhala-anghri-upari — upon the mortar; sthitah — stood; hasan — laughing.

8But Krishna grew angry and broke the pot with a stone; He went into the house, ate His fill of fresh butter and, climbing on the mortar, stood there laughing.

Verse 9

ततो यशोदा स्वसुतस्य कर्म तत्
प्रलापितं चापि हसन्तमूह्य।
बबन्ध दाम्ना तमतो हि नाम्ना
दामोदरात्रैव बभूव प्रेमदः॥९॥

tato yaśodā svasutasya karma tat
pralāpitaṁ cāpi hasantamūhya|
babandha dāmnā tamato hi nāmnā
dāmodarātraiva babhūva premadaḥ||9||

tatah — then; yashoda — Yashoda; sva-sutasya — of her son; karma — the deed; tat — that; pralapitam — the prattle; cha — and; api — also; hasantam — laughing; uhya — perceiving; babandha — bound; damna — with a rope; tam — Him; atah — therefore; hi — indeed; namna — by name; damodara — Damodara; atra — here; eva — indeed; babhuva — became; prema-dah — the giver of love.

9Then Yashoda, perceiving her son's mischief and seeing Him prattle and laugh, bound Him with a rope — and so it was here that He received the name Damodara4, He who bestows love.

Verse 10

दामोदरोऽत्र भगवान् बभञ्ज यमलार्जुनौ।
धान्यं दत्त्वा फलं चात्र बुभुजे फलदेश्वरः॥१०॥

dāmodaro'tra bhagavān babhañja yamalārjunau|
dhānyaṁ dattvā phalaṁ cātra bubhuje phaladeśvaraḥ||10||

damodarah — Damodara; atra — here; bhagavan — the Lord; babhanja — broke; yamala-arjunau — the twin Arjuna trees; dhanyam — grain; dattva — giving; phalam — fruit; cha — and; atra — here; bubhuje — ate; phala-da-ishvarah — the Lord who bestows the fruits.

10Here the Lord Damodara broke the twin Arjuna trees5; here the Lord who bestows all fruits gave away grain and ate fruit6.

Verse 11

अस्य दक्षिणपार्श्वे च गोलोकाख्यं तु गोकुलम्।
बाल्यलीलां हि मात्रापि ह्यकरोदथ स हरिः॥११॥

asya dakṣiṇapārśve ca golokākhyaṁ tu gokulam|
bālyalīlāṁ hi mātrāpi hyakarodatha sa hariḥ||11||

asya — of this; dakshina-parshve — on the south side; cha — and; goloka-akhyam — called Goloka; tu — indeed; gokulam — Gokula; balya-lilam — childhood pastimes; hi — indeed; matra — with His mother; api — also; hi — indeed; akarot — performed; atha — and; sah — He; harih — Hari.

11To the south of this lies Gokula, which is called Goloka; here Hari played His childhood games with His mother.

Verse 12

गोपेश्वरं देवमत्र पश्य सर्वेश्वरेश्वर।
सप्तसामुद्रकं कुण्डमत्र भुवनपावनम्॥१२॥

gopeśvaraṁ devamatra paśya sarveśvareśvara|
saptasāmudrakaṁ kuṇḍamatra bhuvanapāvanam||12||

gopeshvaram — Gopeshvara; devam — the god; atra — here; pashya — behold; sarva-ishvara-ishvara — O Lord of all lords; sapta-samudrakam — Sapta-samudra; kundam — the pond; atra — here; bhuvana-pavanam — purifying the worlds.

12Behold here the god Gopeshvara7, O Lord of all lords, and here the pond Sapta-samudra, which purifies the worlds.

Verse 13

आयानस्य गृहं ग्रामे पश्चिमे रसपूर्वकम्।
आनन्दाख्यो गोपकोऽप्यवसत्तस्यापि दक्षिणे॥१३॥

āyānasya gṛhaṁ grāme paścime rasapūrvakam|
ānandākhyo gopako'pyavasattasyāpi dakṣiṇe||13||

ayanasya — of Ayana; griham — the house; grame — in the village; pashchime — to the west; rasa-purvakam — full of rasa; ananda-akhyah — named Ananda; gopakah — a cowherd; api — also; avasat — lived; tasya — of it; api — too; dakshine — to the south.

13In the village to the west is the house of Ayana8, full of rasa; to the south of it lived a cowherd named Ananda.

Verse 14

उपनन्दगृहं ग्राममध्ये कृष्णसुखप्रदम्।
अस्य पश्चिमभागे च रावणस्य तपोवनम्॥१४॥

upanandagṛhaṁ grāmamadhye kṛṣṇasukhapradam|
asya paścimabhāge ca rāvaṇasya tapovanam||14||

upananda-griham — the house of Upananda; grama-madhye — in the middle of the village; krishna-sukha-pradam — that gave joy to Krishna; asya — of it; pashchima-bhage — on the western side; cha — and; ravanasya — of Ravana; tapah-vanam — the grove of austerities.

14In the middle of the village is the house of Upananda, which gave joy to Krishna, and on its western side is the grove where Ravana performed austerities.

Verse 15

दुर्वाससो मुनेः कृष्ण आश्रमं ह्युत्तरेऽस्य च।
अस्यापि निकटे लोहवनं बिल्ववनं प्रभो॥१५॥

durvāsaso muneḥ kṛṣṇa āśramaṁ hyuttare'sya ca|
asyāpi nikaṭe lohavanaṁ bilvavanaṁ prabho||15||

durvasasah — of Durvasa; muneh — the sage; krishna — O Krishna; ashramam — the hermitage; hi — indeed; uttare — to the north; asya — of it; cha — and; asya — of it; api — too; nikate — near; loha-vanam — Lohavana; bilva-vanam — Bilvavana; prabho — O Lord.

15To the north of it, O Krishna, is the hermitage of the sage Durvasa, and near it, O Lord, are Lohavana and Bilvavana.

Verse 16

अत्रापि पश्य नन्दस्य कृष्णं क्रीडयतः सुखम्।
बाल्यलीलारसं तस्मै ददाति परमाद्भुतम्॥१६॥

atrāpi paśya nandasya kṛṣṇaṁ krīḍayataḥ sukham|
bālyalīlārasaṁ tasmai dadāti paramādbhutam||16||

atra — here; api — also; pashya — behold; nandasya — of Nanda; krishnam — Krishna; kridayatah — playing with; sukham — happily; balya-lila-rasam — the rasa of childhood pastimes; tasmai — to him; dadati — gives; parama-adbhutam — most wonderful.

16Behold this place too: here Nanda would happily play with Krishna, and He gave him the most wonderful rasa of His childhood pastimes.

Verse 17

मेघागमं च दृष्ट्वा स नन्द आह सुगोपिकाम्।
कृष्णमादाय मद्गेहेश्वर्यै शीघ्रं समर्पय॥१७॥

meghāgamaṁ ca dṛṣṭvā sa nanda āha sugopikām|
kṛṣṇamādāya madgeheśvaryai śīghraṁ samarpaya||17||

megha-agamam — the coming of clouds; cha — and; drishtva — seeing; sah — he; nandah — Nanda; aha — said; su-gopikam — to a lovely gopi; krishnam — Krishna; adaya — taking; mat-geha-ishvaryai — to the mistress of my house; shighram — quickly; samarpaya — hand over.

17Seeing the clouds gathering, Nanda said to a lovely gopi, 'Take Krishna and quickly bring Him to the mistress of my house.'9

Verse 18

सापि तं स्वाङ्कमारोप्य चुम्ब्य चानन्दविह्वला।
गाढमालिङ्गिता तेन विस्मिता विवशाभवत्॥१८॥

sāpi taṁ svāṅkamāropya cumbya cānandavihvalā|
gāḍhamāliṅgitā tena vismitā vivaśābhavat||18||

sa — she; api — and; tam — Him; sva-ankam — on her lap; aropya — placing; chumbya — kissing; cha — and; ananda-vihvala — overwhelmed with bliss; gadham — tightly; alingita — embraced; tena — by Him; vismita — amazed; vivasha — helpless; abhavat — became.

18She set Him on her lap and kissed Him, beside herself with bliss; and when He held her tightly in His arms, she was overcome with wonder and left quite helpless."

Verse 19

श्रुत्वा कृष्णरसोल्लासं बालकस्यैव वैभवम्।
गौरकृष्णः कृष्णदासं प्रेम्णालिङ्गितवान् स्वयम्॥१९॥

śrutvā kṛṣṇarasollāsaṁ bālakasyaiva vaibhavam|
gaurakṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇadāsaṁ premṇāliṅgitavān svayam||19||

shrutva — hearing; krishna-rasa-ullasam — the exultation of Krishna's rasa; balakasya — of the Child; eva — indeed; vaibhavam — the glory; gaura-krishnah — Gaura-Krishna; krishnadasam — Krishnadasa; premna — with love; alingitavan — embraced; svayam — Himself.

19Hearing of this exultation of Krishna's rasa, of the glory of the Child, Gaura-Krishna Himself lovingly embraced Krishnadasa.

Verse 20

अत्र पश्य च गोविन्द गोपालचरितं शुभम्।
गोचारणगतेनात्र कुण्डं च हरिणा कृतम्॥२०॥

atra paśya ca govinda gopālacaritaṁ śubham|
gocāraṇagatenātra kuṇḍaṁ ca hariṇā kṛtam||20||

atra — here; pashya — behold; cha — and; govinda — O Govinda; gopala-charitam — the deed of Gopala; shubham — auspicious; go-charana-gatena — who had come to graze the cows; atra — here; kundam — a pond; cha — and; harina — by Hari; kritam — was made.

20"Behold this too, O Govinda: here is an auspicious deed of Gopala — this pond was made by Hari when He came here to graze the cows.

Verse 21

अत्रैव चोपनन्दोऽपि नन्दमाहूय सुन्दरः।
गोपैः परिवृतो युक्तिं कृत्वा कृष्णसुखाय च॥२१॥

atraiva copanando'pi nandamāhūya sundaraḥ|
gopaiḥ parivṛto yuktiṁ kṛtvā kṛṣṇasukhāya ca||21||

atra — here; eva — indeed; cha — and; upanandah — Upananda; api — also; nandam — Nanda; ahuya — summoning; sundarah — the good; gopaih — by the cowherds; parivritah — surrounded; yuktim — counsel; kritva — taking; krishna-sukhaya — for Krishna's welfare; cha — and.

21Here also the good Upananda, surrounded by the cowherds, summoned Nanda and, taking counsel for Krishna's welfare,

Verse 22

सव्रजः शकटमारुह्य रामकृष्णसमन्वितः।
ययौ भद्रकभाण्डीरं द्वौ मासौ तत्र चावसत्॥२२॥

savrajaḥ śakaṭamāruhya rāmakṛṣṇasamanvitaḥ|
yayau bhadrakabhāṇḍīraṁ dvau māsau tatra cāvasat||22||

sa-vrajah — with all Vraja; shakatam — the carts; aruhya — mounting; rama-krishna-samanvitah — together with Rama and Krishna; yayau — went; bhadraka-bhandiram — to Bhadraka and Bhandira; dvau masau — two months; tatra — there; cha — and; avasat — dwelt.

22mounted the carts with all Vraja, together with Rama and Krishna, and went to Bhadraka and Bhandira10; there they lived for two months."

Thus ends the sixth sarga, "Beholding Mahavana and Other Places" (Mahavana-adi-darshana), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Putana: the demoness who tried to poison the infant Krishna with her breast; the cart beneath which Krishna lay He overturned with His little foot; Trinavarta: the whirlwind demon (Bhagavata Purana 10.6–7).
  2. Garga: the priest of the Yadus, who secretly named Krishna and Balarama (Bhagavata Purana 10.8).
  3. The reading of this line is a conjectural restoration.
  4. Damodara: "He whose belly (udara) is bound with a rope (dama)" (Bhagavata Purana 10.9).
  5. The twin Arjuna trees: Nalakuvara and Manigriva, sons of Kubera, cursed by Narada; Krishna, tied to the mortar, uprooted them (Bhagavata Purana 10.10).
  6. An allusion to the fruit-seller to whom the child Krishna gave a handful of grain, and who filled His hands with fruit in return (Bhagavata Purana 10.11).
  7. Gopeshvara ("Lord of the Cowherds"): Shiva, worshipped in Vraja as the guardian (kshetrapala) of that land; tradition says he took the form of a gopi to enter the rasa dance.
  8. Ayana: the cowherd who, by tradition, was considered Radha's husband.
  9. Compare the opening of Jayadeva's Gita-govinda, where Nanda, seeing the clouds, bids Radha take Krishna home. The rapture of the gopi holding the Child Krishna is pure prema, spiritual love without a trace of the worldly.
  10. Bhadraka and Bhandira: two of the twelve forests of Vraja (see sarga 3).
